source.title: First Exit Time Analysis of Stochastic Gradient Descent Under Heavy-Tailed Gradient Noise
source.authors: T. Nguyen; Umut Simsekli; M. Gürbüzbalaban; G. Richard

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes first-exit-time approximation for SGD and discusses wide minima as a proxy for generalization. Its experiments measure exit-time error, not training or test error or any other outcome named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on generalization and wide minima, but does not test the listed claim versions. Its neural-network experiment reports how first-exit-time approximation error varies with step size, depth, and width; this does not measure the generalization gap.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes agreement between discrete and continuous stochastic dynamics through first exit times. It reports no held-out performance or sharpness–generalization-gap comparison. Its discussion of wider minima generalizing better is background motivation, not a test of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under the stated assumptions, the authors derive explicit step-size conditions for discrete dynamics to approximate continuous-time first-exit behavior, with dependence on problem and algorithm parameters, and illustrate this using synthetic and neural-network experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies theoretical and empirical first-exit-time approximation under Brownian and heavy-tailed Lévy noise; it does not use the original studies' generalization measurements or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that exit-time approximation error depends on step size, noise amplitude, Gaussian-noise variance, dimension, and network width and depth.

fits_no_version.finding: For the tested fully connected MNIST networks, exit-time approximation error increases with step size, with steeper increases for larger width and depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger tested networks require smaller step sizes for discrete SGD to approximate the metastability behavior of its continuous-time model.

record.problems: The neural-network experiment reports first-exit-time approximation rather than generalization; the Figure 3 discussion gives qualitative trends without numerical values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were reported. Synthetic-model exit-time experiments and theoretical bounds concern continuous/discrete process approximation, not the listed generalization outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under different tuning recipes.
Large-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance tracking training–test gaps and ranking them against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The discretization caveat concerns a proposed dynamical explanation of SGD, not evidence against any listed generalization version. No claim-relevant results are missing from the record.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Test error as network width increases past interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the training-test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD until at least 90% accuracy, then first exit times measured
rows.operation_detail: Measured first-exit-time approximation error while varying step size and network depth.

conditions.value: no explicit Gaussian or Lévy noise

rows.measure: Error in first exit time between the discretized process and its continuous-time approximation
rows.value: The error behaves similarly to Figure 2(a); its slope increases for larger depth.
rows.note: This is an exit-time approximation result, not a measure of generalization error.
rows.check: The qualitative depth trend is correctly recorded, but exit-time approximation error cannot establish any claim version. The at-least-90% accuracy criterion selects a starting neighborhood; it is not a reported generalization result.
